records.text: The Office of the Secretary of Defense said it could not respond to the FOIA request within the statutory 20-day period because unusual circumstances affected its ability to process the request quickly.
records.speaker: Office of the Secretary of Defense

appearances.snippet: Although we have already begun processing your request, we will not be able to respond within the FOIA's 20-day statutory time period as there are unusual circumstances which impact our ability to quickly process your request.

verification.notes: The primary episode reads the Office of the Secretary of Defense response stating that processing had begun but a response could not be made within FOIA’s 20-day period because unusual circumstances affected prompt processing. The statutory FOIA text independently confirms the 20-day determination period and written-notice extension for unusual circumstances.

records.text: The FOIA response said unusual circumstances could include the need to consult one or more other agencies or Department of War components with a substantial interest in the determination or subject matter of the records.
records.speaker: Office of the Secretary of Defense

appearances.snippet: Quest, so A and B is not us, C, the need for consultation with one or more other agencies or the Department of War Components having a substantial interest in either the determination or the subject matter of the records.

verification.notes: The episode reads the response’s consultation category. The official FOIA statute defines unusual circumstances to include consultation with another agency having a substantial interest or among two or more agency components with substantial subject-matter interest, matching the cited language apart from the department’s current naming convention.
